description: ADOPT nbgrader's cell-level metadata schema and hidden-test mechanics in place of praxis's parallel invention, and make `nbgrader validate` the authoritative gate instead of bespoke pytest. Decision D10 in rosetta/strategy/DECISIONS.md. THE FINDING: nbgrader (github.com/jupyter/nbgrader, 1,369 stars, BSD-3-Clause, pushed 2026-07-31) already ships the mature hidden-test abstraction that praxis's tests/test_notebooks.py + praxis/checks.py reimplement — `### BEGIN HIDDEN TESTS` / `### END HIDDEN TESTS` and `### BEGIN SOLUTION` / `### END SOLUTION` region stripping, with `nbgrader generate_assignment` producing the learner-facing notebook from a single authored source — plus a CELL-LEVEL METADATA SCHEMA for graded regions (`metadata.nbgrader`: `grade`, `solution`, `locked`, `task`, `grade_id`, `points`, `schema_version`, `checksum`) that is the de-facto standard across the Jupyter grading ecosystem. Praxis's `metadata.praxis` and its `<slug>.checks.json` sidecar are a PARALLEL invention of the same thing. Adopting the schema buys interop with every tool that speaks nbgrader (JupyterHub course workflows, ngshare, otter-grader's nbgrader compatibility), and turns a bespoke grader into a standard one. WHAT PRAXIS KEEPS — and this is the point of the decision: the genuinely novel half is CONSTRUCTION (subject -> curriculum -> rubric-shaped scaffold -> AI-filled tutorial -> auto-authored checks). nbgrader has ZERO content generation and no OSS competitor exists for that pipeline. So praxis becomes an nbgrader-schema PRODUCER: praxis/checks.py stops inventing a format and starts emitting nbgrader cells. HONEST GAPS TO SETTLE, NOT PAPER OVER: (1) nbgrader is code-centric — its schema has no native equivalent of praxis's `choice` (multiple-choice) and `short` (model-graded free text) checks, so those must be carried as a DOCUMENTED, NAMESPACED praxis extension that an nbgrader-only consumer ignores cleanly, never as a silent fork of the schema; (2) praxis's load-bearing anti-fabrication rule — a code check's reference `solution` is run against its own `test` in a subprocess before the set may be written (`verify_code=True`) — maps onto nbgrader's own validate semantics and must be PRESERVED, not dropped because the schema changed; (3) the server-side boundary must survive: `learner_check()` is the only way a check reaches a client, a locked section serves no checks at all, and `POST /api/study/<rel>` answers 423 — the answer key must NOT end up in the learner-facing notebook just because nbgrader's release format keeps everything in one file. Scope: praxis/checks.py, praxis/progress.py, praxis/rubric.py, praxis/construct.py, tests/, docs/explanation/notebook-rubric.md, pyproject.toml. See rosetta/strategy/DECISIONS.md D10.
warmup: echo '--- the parallel invention to retire: praxis metadata + the sidecar checkset ---'; grep -rn 'metadata.*praxis\|checks_path\|GATED_SECTIONS' praxis/checks.py praxis/construct.py praxis/rubric.py | head -20
echo '--- the reimplemented hidden-test / gate logic ---'; sed -n '1,40p' tests/test_notebooks.py
echo '--- the load-bearing rule that must survive: solution run against its own test ---'; grep -n 'verify_code\|subprocess\|def checkset_failures\|def learner_check' praxis/checks.py | head
echo '--- nbgrader schema reference (offline: read the vendored notes if present) ---'; ls docs/ | head -20

userStories.title: Emit nbgrader's cell-level metadata schema for graded regions
acceptanceCriteria: Constructed and scaffolded notebooks carry nbgrader's cell-level schema on graded regions — `metadata.nbgrader` with the real field names and value semantics (`grade`, `solution`, `locked`, `task`, `grade_id`, `points`, `schema_version`, `checksum`) and the real cell kinds (autograded answer, autograder tests, manually graded answer, read-only, manually graded task) — pinned against nbgrader's published schema version rather than a hand-copied approximation.

`grade_id` values are stable and unique within a notebook and are the identity a recorded outcome keys on, so an outcome survives a notebook being reconstructed (the current sidecar's implicit ordering identity is replaced by a real id, not by a second one).

praxis's two non-nbgrader check kinds — `choice` and `short` — are carried as an explicitly NAMESPACED praxis extension alongside `metadata.nbgrader` (documented in docs/explanation/notebook-rubric.md as an extension, with the statement that nbgrader itself is code-centric and has no equivalent), so an nbgrader-only consumer reads the graded cells correctly and ignores the extension rather than choking on a mutated schema.

A migration path exists for the notebooks already on disk: the 24 seed notebooks that carry a `<slug>.checks.json` today are converted to the nbgrader schema by a documented, idempotent, re-runnable pass, and a converted notebook grades identically to the way it graded before (a test asserts equivalence on at least one real converted seed, not a fixture).

Gate green: `python3 -m pytest -q tests/` passes, including a test that a constructed notebook's graded cells validate against nbgrader's schema and that the praxis extension round-trips without touching `metadata.nbgrader`.
userStories.notes: python3 -m pytest -q tests/: 908 passed, 1 skipped; migration converted 24 seed notebooks and verified 168 graded cells with unique stable grade_id values.

userStories.title: Adopt nbgrader's hidden-test and solution-region mechanics, retiring the reimplementation
acceptanceCriteria: Authoring uses nbgrader's delimiters — `### BEGIN SOLUTION` / `### END SOLUTION` and `### BEGIN HIDDEN TESTS` / `### END HIDDEN TESTS` — as the single source form, and the learner-facing notebook is DERIVED from it by nbgrader's own release/generate mechanics rather than by praxis code that reimplements the same stripping.

The bespoke stripping/hidden-test logic in `tests/test_notebooks.py` and `praxis/checks.py` is DELETED, not left beside the adopted mechanism — a test asserts there is exactly one implementation of solution-region and hidden-test removal in the tree, so the two cannot drift.

The server-side boundary survives the format change and is proved: the learner-facing artifact contains NO hidden tests, no reference `solution`, no `answer`/`expected`, and a locked section still serves nothing at all; `learner_check()` (or its successor) remains the only path by which a check reaches a client, and `POST /api/study/<rel>` still answers 423 for an unreached section. A test asserts the released notebook is free of every stripped region by content inspection, not by trusting the generator.

The load-bearing anti-fabrication rule is preserved under the new format: a code check's reference `solution` is still executed against its own `test` before the graded cells may be written (today's `verify_code=True` subprocess run), so 'auto-graded' can still never mean 'asserts nothing'; a set failing it is still never written.

Gate green: `python3 -m pytest -q tests/` passes, including a test that a hidden-test region is present in the source notebook, absent from the released one, and still enforced when the learner's answer is graded.
userStories.notes: uv run --extra dev pytest -q tests/: 909 passed, 1 skipped; nbgrader release test verified solution and hidden-test regions are absent from the learner artifact and code grading still distinguishes correct from incorrect answers.

userStories.title: Make `nbgrader validate` the authoritative gate in place of bespoke pytest
acceptanceCriteria: `nbgrader` is a real, pinned dependency (BSD-3-Clause, recorded in `pyproject.toml` with its licence noted alongside the project's other deps), and `nbgrader validate` is the AUTHORITATIVE gate a constructed notebook must pass before it is written — replacing the bespoke pytest assertions that currently stand in for it, not running beside them.

`praxis/rubric.py`'s grader keeps the responsibilities nbgrader does not have (the 8 rubric sections, placeholder detection, real `https://` Resources URLs, the ✅ badge, size and code-cell counts) and DELEGATES everything nbgrader validates (graded-cell wellformedness, hidden-test execution, solution/test agreement); the split is documented in `CLAUDE.md` so a future contributor cannot reintroduce a parallel check.

`.chief/verify.sh` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` both run the nbgrader gate path-scoped in the same place they run `pytest tests/` today, and stay mirrors of one another (the repo's stated rule: change one, change the other).

A validate failure produces a message specific enough to act on and is fed back to the model as the repair prompt exactly as the grader's own sentences are today — the repair loop is preserved, only its source of truth changed.

Gate green: `python3 -m pytest -q tests/` passes, `nbgrader validate` passes on the converted seed notebooks, and a test asserts a deliberately broken graded cell is rejected by `nbgrader validate` and never written.
